issues_confirmed.detail: The merge test is a strict `dist < minDist`, but it runs AFTER resolveCollision (Fruits.ts:60-69) has separated the pair by exactly `minDist - dist`, leaving dist == minDist. With dx exactly 0 (nx = dx/dist = 0, so the x correction is a no-op) there is no floating-point slop to rescue it. dx is exactly 0 for normal play because dropFruit (GameCanvas.tsx:21-28) always reuses the same clamped fruitDropX and a dx==0 collision imparts no vx.
issues_confirmed.verified_by: Re-derived Fruits.ts + the draw() body headlessly and ran 600 frames (10s). 2 Cherries at identical x: 0 merges, 500 frames sitting at exactly-touching. 2 Watermelons at identical x: 0 merges, 506 near-misses. 2 Cherries with a 5px x-offset: merges to Strawberry. 4 Cherries at identical x: only 1 merge, and only because a third body nudges x.

issues_confirmed.detail: Both indices are added to mergedIndices unconditionally, but `if (nextIndex < fruitTypes.length)` then pushes no replacement, so two merging Watermelons (the top tier) both delete themselves. Coupled to the bug above: applying the `+ 0.5` slop fix alone turns this from rare into the normal ending.
issues_confirmed.verified_by: Headless replication. 2 Watermelons with a 12px x-offset: 1 merge, board ends EMPTY. With the proposed `dist < minDist + 0.5` slop, 2 Watermelons at identical x also merge to an EMPTY board.

issues_confirmed.detail: dt is computed from raw rAF timestamps with no clamp. rAF pauses in a background tab, so the first frame on return carries a multi-second dt, and the floor bounce in Fruits.ts:39-43 multiplies the inflated vy by -0.4 — the body gains energy and tunnels through anything between.
issues_confirmed.verified_by: Headless: a single dt = 3.0 frame moves a falling Cherry to y = 788 and leaves vy = -600.

issues_confirmed.detail: A viewport-sized `absolute inset-0 z-10` div sits over the canvas. handleCanvasClick (page.tsx:10-14) casts e.target to HTMLCanvasElement, but e.target is the overlay, so getBoundingClientRect() returns the viewport rect rather than the canvas rect (canvas is w-[90vw] max-w-[800px] centred in a p-4 flex box, GameCanvas.tsx:126-127). At 1280px the canvas occupies roughly x in [240,1040], so drops land ~240px right of the cursor and anything past x~800 saturates on the clamp at GameCanvas.tsx:24. TypeScript cannot catch the bad cast because e.target is typed EventTarget. The overlay also swallows mousemove, so the canvas listener at GameCanvas.tsx:58 never fires, mouseX stays null, and the ghost preview at GameCanvas.tsx:69-74 is dead code.
issues_confirmed.verified_by: Reading the component tree and the served markup; the overlay has no pointer-events-none and is not an ancestor of the canvas, so mousemove cannot reach it.

issues_confirmed.detail: The effect's only dep is mouseX, and its cleanup (119-122) removes both listeners but never calls cancelAnimationFrame, while draw re-arms itself at line 114. The input bug above is the only thing currently masking this: the moment mousemove reaches the canvas, every mouse movement sets state, re-runs the effect, and spawns another self-perpetuating rAF loop over the same fruitsRef — dozens of concurrent loops each applying gravity to one shared array. Fixing the overlay without this makes the game dramatically worse.
issues_confirmed.verified_by: Reading the effect: no rAF id is captured anywhere in the file, and the returned cleanup contains only two removeEventListener calls.
